input.question: Why aren’t we allowed to lower the salaries of politicians? So that we can be sure that they are running not for money but because they really want to serve?
input.ground_truth: Mostly because it would become a tool to control the have-nots. Lower the the salaries of politicians until it a burden even for those who want to serve. Net result is that the only people who would run wouldn't be the people who want to serve, but the people who are financially able. Side note. Most of the money politician make come from things other than their salary. Book deals, speeches, etc...

If you give them lots of candy (like a big salary), some friends might help just for the candy, not because they love helping.

But if you don’t give them any candy at all, some friends might not want to help because they need candy to buy toys or snacks.

So, to be fair and make sure everyone can help if they want, you give everyone the *same* amount of candy—enough for them to live on, but not so much that they only help for the candy.

So, we don’t just lower politicians’ salaries because then good people who really want to help might not be able to do the job, and it might not be fair. We want people to help because they care, but we also want to make sure they can live okay while they help.
